explainer_reply:
Looking at these examples, the activations are all weak (1-4) and highly diffuse across many contexts. Examining the highlighted tokens, a clear pattern emerges: they are dominated by high-frequency function words — "of" (examples 3, 8, 11, 20, 24, 25, 27, 28, 30), "a" (10, 12, 14, 20, 22, 34), "and" (4, 10, 12, 14, 15, 34), "the", "in", "as", "than", "to", "by". Many highlights also fall within extremely common collocations ("sense of the word", "as well as", "host of", "amount of", "set of", "big deal", "more than", "to be constructed"). The few content words highlighted ("map", "movie", "teacher", "dollars") appear embedded in these ordinary phrases, and even punctuation tokens (commas, periods, hyphens) are occasionally marked.

[EXPLANATION]: The neuron fires weakly on common English function words — prepositions, articles, and conjunctions such as "of", "a", "the", "and", "in" — typically as part of frequent collocations and mid-sentence phrases, with no strong topical or semantic specificity.
